source.text: הִרְאַנִי֮ יְהוָה֒ וְהִנֵּ֗ה שְׁנֵי֙ דּוּדָאֵ֣י תְאֵנִ֔ים מוּעָדִ֕ים לִפְנֵ֖י הֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֑ה אַחֲרֵ֣י הַגְל֣וֹת נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֣ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֡ל אֶת־יְכָנְיָ֣הוּ בֶן־יְהוֹיָקִ֣ים מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָה֩ וְאֶת־שָׂרֵ֨י יְהוּדָ֜ה וְאֶת־הֶחָרָ֤שׁ וְאֶת־הַמַּסְגֵּר֙ מִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַיְבִאֵ֖ם בָּבֶֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Showed me Yahweh, and behold, two baskets of figs placed before [the] temple of Yahweh, after [the] exiling [by] Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon [of] Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah, and [the] princes of Judah, and the craftsman and the smith from Jerusalem, and he brought them [to] Babylon.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} showed me, and look, two baskets of figs set before the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, after Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon had exiled Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah, and the princes of Judah, and the craftsmen and the smiths, from Jerusalem, and had brought them [to] Babylon.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} showed me two baskets of figs set in front of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. This was after Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon had taken Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah into exile from Jerusalem, together with the officials of Judah, the craftsmen and the smiths, and had brought them to Babylon.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} showed me a vision. I saw two baskets of figs that had been put in front of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. This happened after Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon had taken Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, the king of Judah, away from Jerusalem as a captive. Nebuchadrezzar took him to Babylon, together with the leaders of Judah and the skilled workers and metalworkers.

es.L: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me mostró, y he aquí dos cestas de higos puestas delante del templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, después que Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, había llevado cautivo a Jeconías hijo de Joacim, rey de Judá, y a los príncipes de Judá, y a los artesanos y a los herreros, de Jerusalén, y los había llevado a Babilonia.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me mostró dos cestas de higos puestas delante del templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Esto fue después de que Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, se llevó cautivo de Jerusalén a Jeconías hijo de Joacim, rey de Judá, junto con los jefes de Judá, los artesanos y los herreros, y los llevó a Babilonia.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me mostró una visión. Vi dos cestas de higos que habían puesto delante del templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Esto pasó después de que Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, se llevó prisionero de Jerusalén a Jeconías hijo de Joacim, el rey de Judá. Nabucodorosor lo llevó a Babilonia junto con los dirigentes de Judá y los trabajadores especializados y los herreros.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me fit voir, et voici, deux paniers de figues placés devant le temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, après que Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, eut déporté de Jérusalem Jéchonias fils de Joïaqim, roi de Juda, et les princes de Juda, et les artisans et les forgerons, et les eut emmenés [à] Babylone.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me fit voir deux paniers de figues placés devant le temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. C’était après que Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, eut emmené en exil loin de Jérusalem Jéchonias fils de Joïaqim, roi de Juda, avec les chefs de Juda, les artisans et les forgerons, et les eut conduits à Babylone.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a montré une vision. J’ai vu deux paniers de figues qu’on avait posés devant le temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Cela s’est passé après que Nabuchodonosor, le roi de Babylone, a emmené de Jérusalem comme prisonnier Jéchonias, fils de Joïaqim, le roi de Juda. Nabuchodonosor l’a emmené à Babylone avec les chefs de Juda, les artisans et ceux qui travaillaient les métaux.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alinionyesha, na tazama, vikapu viwili vya tini vilivyowekwa mbele ya hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, baada ya Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli kumchukua mateka Yekonia mwana wa Yehoyakimu mfalme wa Yuda, na wakuu wa Yuda, na mafundi na wahunzi, kutoka Yerusalemu, na kuwaleta [mpaka] Babeli.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alinionyesha vikapu viwili vya tini vilivyowekwa mbele ya hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Hii ilikuwa baada ya Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli kumchukua Yekonia mwana wa Yehoyakimu mfalme wa Yuda kutoka Yerusalemu kwenda uhamishoni, pamoja na maafisa wa Yuda, mafundi na wahunzi, akawaleta Babeli.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alinionyesha maono. Niliona vikapu viwili vya tini vilivyokuwa vimewekwa mbele ya hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Hii ilitokea baada ya Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli kumchukua Yekonia mwana wa Yehoyakimu, mfalme wa Yuda, kutoka Yerusalemu kama mateka. Nebukadreza alimpeleka Babeli pamoja na viongozi wa Yuda, mafundi stadi na wafua vyuma.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho tôi thấy, và kìa, có hai giỏ trái vả đặt trước đền thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, sau khi Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn đã bắt Giê-chô-nia con trai Giê-hô-gia-kim, vua Giu-đa, cùng các quan trưởng Giu-đa, thợ thủ công và thợ rèn, lưu đày khỏi Giê-ru-sa-lem và đem họ về Ba-by-lôn.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho tôi thấy hai giỏ trái vả đặt trước đền thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Việc này xảy ra sau khi Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn đã bắt Giê-chô-nia con trai Giê-hô-gia-kim, vua Giu-đa, đi lưu đày khỏi Giê-ru-sa-lem, cùng với các quan chức Giu-đa, thợ thủ công và thợ rèn, và đem họ về Ba-by-lôn.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho tôi thấy một khải tượng. Tôi thấy hai giỏ trái vả được đặt trước đền thờ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Việc này xảy ra sau khi Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn đã bắt Giê-chô-nia con trai Giê-hô-gia-kim, vua Giu-đa, đem khỏi Giê-ru-sa-lem làm tù binh. Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa đem vua ấy về Ba-by-lôn, cùng với các nhà lãnh đạo Giu-đa, các thợ lành nghề và thợ kim loại.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 보여 주셨는데, 보아라, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전 앞에 무화과 두 바구니가 놓여 있었다. 그때는 바빌론 왕 느부갓레살이 유다 왕 여호야김의 아들 여고냐와 유다의 고관들과 장인들과 대장장이들을 예루살렘에서 사로잡아 바빌론으로 데려간 뒤였다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전 앞에 놓인 무화과 두 바구니를 보여 주셨다. 그때는 바빌론 왕 느부갓레살이 유다 왕 여호야김의 아들 여고냐를 유다의 관리들과 장인들과 대장장이들과 함께 예루살렘에서 사로잡아 바빌론으로 데려간 뒤였다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 환상을 보여 주셨다. 나는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전 앞에 무화과 두 바구니가 놓여 있는 것을 보았다. 이 일은 바빌론 왕 느부갓레살이 유다 왕 여호야김의 아들 여고냐를 예루살렘에서 포로로 끌고 간 뒤에 있었다. 느부갓레살은 유다의 지도자들과 솜씨 좋은 일꾼들과 쇠붙이를 다루는 기술자들도 함께 바빌론으로 끌고 갔다.

pt.L: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} me mostrou, e eis dois cestos de figos postos diante do templo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, depois que Nabucodorosor, rei da Babilônia, levou para o exílio Jeconias, filho de Jeoaquim, rei de Judá, e os príncipes de Judá, e os artífices e os ferreiros de Jerusalém, e os trouxe [para a] Babilônia.
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} me mostrou dois cestos de figos colocados diante do templo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}. Isso foi depois que Nabucodorosor, rei da Babilônia, levou Jeconias, filho de Jeoaquim, rei de Judá, para o exílio, de Jerusalém, junto com os oficiais de Judá, os artífices e os ferreiros, e os trouxe para a Babilônia.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} me mostrou uma visão. Vi dois cestos de figos que tinham sido colocados na frente do templo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}. Isso aconteceu depois que Nabucodorosor, rei da Babilônia, levou Jeconias, filho de Jeoaquim, rei de Judá, de Jerusalém como prisioneiro. Nabucodorosor o levou para a Babilônia, junto com os líderes de Judá, os artesãos e os ferreiros.

am.L: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} አሳየኝ፤ እነሆም፣ {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} መቅደስ ፊት የተቀመጡ ሁለት የበለስ ቅርጫቶች [ነበሩ]፤ [ይህም] የባቢሎን ንጉሥ ናቡከደነፆር የይሁዳን ንጉሥ የኢዮአቄምን ልጅ ኢኮንያንን፣ የይሁዳንም አለቆች፣ የእጅ ባለሙያዎችንና አንጥረኞችን ከኢየሩሳሌም ካፈለሰና ወደ ባቢሎን ካመጣቸው በኋላ [ነበረ]።
am.B: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ቤተ መቅደስ ፊት የተቀመጡ ሁለት የበለስ ቅርጫቶች አሳየኝ። ይህም የሆነው የባቢሎን ንጉሥ ናቡከደነፆር የይሁዳን ንጉሥ የኢዮአቄምን ልጅ ኢኮንያንን ከይሁዳ ባለ ሥልጣናት፣ ከእጅ ባለሙያዎችና ከአንጥረኞች ጋር ከኢየሩሳሌም ማርኮ ወደ ባቢሎን ከወሰዳቸው በኋላ ነበር።
am.R: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ራእይ አሳየኝ። {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ቤተ መቅደስ ፊት የተቀመጡ ሁለት የበለስ ቅርጫቶች አየሁ። ይህ የሆነው የባቢሎን ንጉሥ ናቡከደነፆር የይሁዳን ንጉሥ የኢዮአቄምን ልጅ ኢኮንያንን ማርኮ ከኢየሩሳሌም ከወሰደው በኋላ ነበር። ናቡከደነፆር እርሱን፣ የይሁዳን መሪዎች፣ የእጅ ባለሙያዎችንና የብረት ሠራተኞችን ወደ ባቢሎን ወሰዳቸው።

hi.L: {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने मुझे दिखाया, और देखो, {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के मंदिर के सामने अंजीरों की दो टोकरियाँ रखी हुई [थीं]; [यह] उसके बाद [हुआ] जब बाबुल के राजा नबूकदरेस्सर ने यहूदा के राजा यहोयाकीम के पुत्र यकुन्याह को, और यहूदा के हाकिमों को, और कारीगरों और लोहारों को यरूशलेम से बंधुआई में भेज दिया था और उन्हें बाबुल ले आया था।
hi.B: {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने मुझे अंजीरों की दो टोकरियाँ दिखाईं, जो {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के मंदिर के सामने रखी थीं। यह उसके बाद की बात है जब बाबुल का राजा नबूकदरेस्सर यहूदा के राजा यहोयाकीम के पुत्र यकुन्याह को, और उसके साथ यहूदा के अधिकारियों, कारीगरों और लोहारों को, यरूशलेम से बंधुआई में बाबुल ले गया था।
hi.R: {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने मुझे एक दर्शन दिखाया। मैंने अंजीरों की दो टोकरियाँ देखीं, जो {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के मंदिर के सामने रखी गई थीं। यह उसके बाद हुआ जब बाबुल का राजा नबूकदरेस्सर यहूदा के राजा, यहोयाकीम के बेटे यकुन्याह को बंदी बनाकर यरूशलेम से ले गया था। नबूकदरेस्सर उसे, और उसके साथ यहूदा के अगुवों और कुशल कारीगरों और धातु का काम करनेवालों को, बाबुल ले गया।

ru.L: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} показал мне, и вот, две корзины смокв, поставленные перед храмом {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}, после того как Навуходорносор, царь Вавилона, увёл в плен Иехонию, сына Иоакима, царя Иудейского, и князей Иуды, и мастеров, и кузнецов из Иерусалима и привёл их [в] Вавилон.
ru.B: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} показал мне две корзины смокв, поставленные перед храмом {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}. Это было после того, как Навуходорносор, царь Вавилона, увёл из Иерусалима в изгнание Иехонию, сына Иоакима, царя Иуды, вместе с вельможами Иуды, мастерами и кузнецами, и привёл их в Вавилон.
ru.R: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} показал мне видение. Я увидел две корзины инжира, которые были поставлены перед храмом {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}. Это было после того, как Навуходорносор, царь Вавилона, увёл из Иерусалима в плен Иехонию, сына Иоакима, царя Иуды. Навуходорносор увёл его в Вавилон вместе с начальниками Иуды, мастерами и кузнецами.

ja.L: {{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}がわたしに示された。するとなんと、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の神殿の前に、いちじくのかごが二つ置かれていた。[それは]バビロンの王ネブカドネツァルが、ユダの王ヨヤキムの子エコンヤと、ユダの長たちと、職人と鍛冶屋をエルサレムから捕らえ移し、彼らをバビロンに連れて行った後のことである。
ja.B: {{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}は、わたしに、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の神殿の前に置かれた二つのいちじくのかごを示された。それは、バビロンの王ネブカドネツァルが、ユダの王ヨヤキムの子エコンヤを、ユダの高官たちや職人や鍛冶屋と共に、エルサレムから捕囚として連れ去り、バビロンに連れて行った後のことである。
ja.R: {{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}は、わたしに幻を見せてくださいました。わたしは、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の神殿の前に、いちじくの入ったかごが二つ置かれているのを見ました。それは、バビロンの王ネブカドネツァルが、ユダの王でヨヤキムの息子であるヨヤキンを、捕虜にしてエルサレムから連れて行った後のことでした。ネブカドネツァルは、ヨヤキンと一緒に、ユダの指導者たちや、腕のいい職人や、金属を扱う職人たちを、バビロンに連れて行ったのです。

uk.L: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}} показав мені, і ось два кошики смокв, поставлені перед храмом {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}}, після того як Навуходоносор, цар Вавилону, вигнав Єхонію, сина Йоакима, царя Юдеї, і князів Юдеї, і ремісників, і ковалів з Єрусалима, і привів їх [до] Вавилону.
uk.B: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}} показав мені два кошики смокв, поставлені перед храмом {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}}. Це було після того, як Навуходоносор, цар Вавилону, забрав у полон з Єрусалима Єхонію, сина Йоакима, царя Юдеї, разом з урядниками Юдеї, ремісниками й ковалями, і привів їх до Вавилону.
uk.R: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}} дав мені видіння. Я побачив два кошики смокв, які поставили перед храмом {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}}. Це сталося після того, як Навуходоносор, цар Вавилону, забрав з Єрусалима в полон Єхонію, сина Йоакима, царя Юдеї. Навуходоносор забрав його до Вавилону разом з провідниками Юдеї, умілими майстрами й ковалями.

decisions.choice: the LORD showed me: a vision given by God and then explained
alternatives: an ordinary sight that Jeremiah saw at the temple
decisions.reason: The words "the LORD showed me, and look" open visions in Amos (Amos 7:1, 4, 7; 8:1), and the vision of a basket of summer fruit in Amos 8:1-2 is the closest to this one. As in Jeremiah's call (1:11-14), God asks what the prophet sees and then gives its meaning (verses 3-10). Whether the baskets were really standing at the temple or were seen only in the vision, the text does not say.

decisions.choice: set before the temple: placed in front of the sanctuary, perhaps as offerings
alternatives: simply standing there, with no religious purpose
decisions.reason: The verb means to be set in an appointed place. Fruit brought to the sanctuary was usually an offering: the first of the harvest was set down before the LORD (Deuteronomy 26:2-4, 10). The text does not say why the baskets were there; what matters is the contrast between them.

decisions.choice: the exile of 597 BC, when King Jeconiah and Judah's leading men were taken to Babylon
decisions.reason: This is the deportation told in 2 Kings 24:12-16. Jeconiah is the king called Jehoiachin in Kings and Coniah in Jeremiah 22:24; this verse uses the form Jeconiah. Nebuchadrezzar is the form of the Babylonian king's name used in most of Jeremiah, closer to its Babylonian form; Kings and some verses of Jeremiah spell it Nebuchadnezzar. He is the same king. The vision comes after this exile, in the reign of Zedekiah (verse 8).

decisions.choice: the craftsman and the smith: skilled workers, especially metalworkers, as groups
decisions.reason: Both nouns are singular with the article, naming each trade as a whole. The second word comes from a verb meaning "to shut" and may name smiths, makers of locks and fittings, or men who built defenses; see 2 Kings 24:14, which lists the same two groups.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar; Jeconiah; princes (Literal), officials (Balanced), leaders (Readable); craftsmen and smiths (Readable: skilled workers and metalworkers)
decisions.reason: Each name keeps the form this verse uses (see m3). The officials and the two trades are worded as in 2 Kings 24:14-16 and the books' usual wording for princes.

decisions.choice: This was after ...; Readable: showed me a vision; I saw; names Nebuchadrezzar again
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the long verse into sentences. Readable says that this was a vision and names the king again so that "he" is clear.

decisions.choice: Jeconías
decisions.reason: The Hebrew here uses the form Jeconiah, so every level keeps "Jeconías", the published form of Matthew 1:11-12; 22:24 has "Conías" for the same king.

decisions.choice: los príncipes (Literal); los jefes (Balanced); los dirigentes (Readable)
decisions.reason: The *sarim* of Judah are "príncipes" at Literal, as the English says "princes", and leading men at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: Yekonia
decisions.reason: The verse's own form of the king's name (Kings note: Yekonia); 22:24 used the short "Konia" as its Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: "Jéchonias"; "les princes" (L), "les chefs" (B, R); "les artisans et les forgerons"
decisions.reason: Each verse keeps the form of the name its Hebrew uses (Jeconiah here, Coniah in 22:24); the officials and the two trades are worded as 2 Kings 24:12-14 in French.

decisions.choice: first-person vision: "me fit voir" (L, B), "m'a montré" (R)
alternatives: m'a fait voir at every level
decisions.reason: Jeremiah tells what he saw, so French uses the narrative tenses by level, as in 18:3: passé simple at Literal and Balanced, passé composé at Readable.

decisions.choice: "Giê-chô-nia"; "thợ thủ công và thợ rèn" (L, B), "thợ lành nghề và thợ kim loại" (R)
decisions.reason: The name keeps the form this verse's Hebrew uses, published in Matthew 1:11; the craftsmen and smiths take the published words of 2 Kings 24:14, 16 at each level, since this is the same exile.

decisions.choice: "여고냐"; "느부갓레살"
decisions.reason: The terms note keeps each verse's own form of the names: Jeconiah is "여고냐" (Matthew 1:12; 1 Chronicles 3:17), and this verse's Hebrew spells the Babylonian king Nebuchadrezzar.

decisions.choice: "고관들" (L); "관리들" (B); "지도자들" (R) for the princes of Judah
decisions.reason: *sar* is a high official, not a king's son; "방백" is an older church word.

decisions.choice: Jeconias; os artífices e os ferreiros (L, B), os artesãos e os ferreiros (R)
decisions.reason: The king keeps the form this verse gives him (m3), "Jeconias", the form Matthew 1:11 has in Portuguese; it is the Conias of 22:24 and the Joaquim of 2 Kings. The two trades (m4) are worded as 2 Kings 24:14 has them in Portuguese.

decisions.choice: "ናቡከደነፆር" for Nebuchadrezzar and "ኢኮንያን" for Jeconiah
decisions.reason: One Amharic form of the king's name, "ናቡከደነፆር" (2 Kings), for the whole of Jeremiah, whether the Hebrew spells it with r (as here and the English) or with n. Jeconiah is the short Hebrew form of Jehoiachin; "ኢኮንያን" is the form of 1 Chronicles 3:16 and Matthew 1:11 on main, kept apart from "ዮአኪን" (2 Kings).

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Amharic
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the English setting that capitalizes pronouns for God has nothing to change in Amharic; the Amharic text of this chapter has no deity_pronoun spans.

decisions.choice: "የእግዚአብሔር መቅደስ" (Literal), "ቤተ መቅደስ" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew here is the heikhal, the sanctuary building: Literal says "መቅደስ" as the Kings terms list does for heikhal; Balanced and Readable use the everyday word for the temple.

decisions.choice: "Єхонія" for Jeconiah, beside "Конія" in 22:24 and 22:28
decisions.reason: Keeps the two forms of the king's name apart, as the English does.

decisions.choice: प्रभु for both YHWH and Adonai; the divine_name setting tells them apart
decisions.reason: Hindi प्रभु translates both the divine name YHWH and the title Adonai ("Lord"). Wherever the Hebrew has the name, प्रभु stands inside a divine_name span whose alternative is याहवे, so a reader who switches the setting sees which is which; प्रभु outside a span is Adonai. यहोवा (the Old Version's form) is not used. God takes honorific plural agreement (वे, उन्होंने) in both options. Recorded once for this block of Jeremiah (24-31).

decisions.choice: नबूकदरेस्सर; यकुन्याह; यहोयाकीम; हाकिम (L), अधिकारी (B), अगुवे (R); कारीगर और लोहार
decisions.reason: Jeremiah spells the Babylonian king two ways, and the terms note keeps each as the Hebrew has it: this verse's Nebuchadrezzar is नबूकदरेस्सर, kept apart from नबूकदनेस्सर (2 Kings 24-25, Daniel, and Jeremiah 27-29). Jeconiah is यकुन्याह as in 1 Chronicles 3:16 and Esther 2:6. The princes (sarim) are हाकिम at L, अधिकारी at B and अगुवे at R, as through the book (1:18), and the craftsmen and smiths कारीगर और लोहार, as 2 Kings 24:12-16 has them.

decisions.choice: Навуходорносор
decisions.reason: The Hebrew here spells the king's name with r (Nebuchadrezzar), and the English keeps that spelling apart from Nebuchadnezzar; Russian keeps the two apart too, Навуходорносор for this form and Навуходоносор (as Kings and Daniel) for the other.

decisions.choice: Иехония; князья (L), вельможи (B), начальники (R)
decisions.reason: Jeconiah takes the form of 2 Kings 24 and 1 Chronicles 3 in this translation; the king's officials (sarim) take the three forms settled for Ezra and Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah's first-person report of the vision: plain (L, B), です・ます (R), with light respect forms for the LORD ("示された", "見せてくださいました"); vehinneh "するとなんと" (L), as 13:7.
decisions.reason: The JER narrative rule.

decisions.choice: Yekhonyahu "エコンヤ" (L, B), "ヨヤキン" (R, as EST 2:6 and 2 Kings 24); sarei Yehudah "ユダの長たち" (L), "高官たち" (B), "指導者たち" (R); hecharash vehammasger "職人と鍛冶屋" (L, B), "腕のいい職人や、金属を扱う職人たち" (R), as 2 Kings 24:14.
decisions.reason: JER conventions for Jeconiah; Readable uses the king's best-known name, kept apart from ヨヤキム.

source.text: הַדּ֣וּד אֶחָ֗ד תְּאֵנִים֙ טֹב֣וֹת מְאֹ֔ד כִּתְאֵנֵ֖י הַבַּכֻּר֑וֹת וְהַדּ֣וּד אֶחָ֗ד תְּאֵנִים֙ רָע֣וֹת מְאֹ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־תֵֽאָכַ֖לְנָה מֵרֹֽעַ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: The basket one, figs good very, like [the] figs of the first-ripe; and the basket one, figs bad very, which not will be eaten from badness.

en.L: One basket [had] very good figs, like the first-ripe figs; and the other basket [had] very bad figs, which could not be eaten because of [their] badness.
en.B: One basket held very good figs, like figs that ripen first; the other basket held very bad figs, so bad that they could not be eaten.
en.R: One basket had very good figs, like the first figs of the season. The other basket had very bad figs. They were so bad that no one could eat them.

es.L: Una cesta [tenía] higos muy buenos, como los higos primerizos; y la otra cesta [tenía] higos muy malos, que no se podían comer de tan malos.
es.B: Una cesta tenía higos muy buenos, como los higos que maduran primero; la otra cesta tenía higos muy malos, tan malos que no se podían comer.
es.R: Una cesta tenía higos muy buenos, como los primeros higos de la temporada. La otra cesta tenía higos muy malos. Eran tan malos que nadie podía comérselos.

fr.L: Un panier [avait] de très bonnes figues, comme les figues de la première récolte ; et l’autre panier [avait] de très mauvaises figues, qu’on ne pouvait pas manger tant elles étaient mauvaises.
fr.B: Un panier contenait de très bonnes figues, comme les figues précoces ; l’autre panier contenait de très mauvaises figues, si mauvaises qu’on ne pouvait pas les manger.
fr.R: Dans un panier, il y avait de très bonnes figues, comme les premières figues de la saison. Dans l’autre panier, il y avait de très mauvaises figues. Elles étaient si mauvaises que personne ne pouvait les manger.

sw.L: Kikapu kimoja [kilikuwa na] tini nzuri sana, kama tini za malimbuko; na kikapu kingine [kilikuwa na] tini mbaya sana, zisizoweza kuliwa kwa sababu ya ubaya [wake].
sw.B: Kikapu kimoja kilikuwa na tini nzuri sana, kama tini zinazoiva kwanza; kikapu kingine kilikuwa na tini mbaya sana, mbaya kiasi kwamba hazikuweza kuliwa.
sw.R: Kikapu kimoja kilikuwa na tini nzuri sana, kama tini za kwanza za msimu. Kikapu kingine kilikuwa na tini mbaya sana. Zilikuwa mbaya kiasi kwamba hakuna mtu angeweza kuzila.

vi.L: Một giỏ [có] trái vả rất tốt, như trái vả chín đầu mùa; còn giỏ kia [có] trái vả rất xấu, xấu đến nỗi không thể ăn được.
vi.B: Một giỏ đựng những trái vả rất ngon, như trái vả chín sớm đầu mùa; giỏ kia đựng những trái vả rất xấu, xấu đến nỗi không ăn được.
vi.R: Một giỏ có những trái vả rất ngon, giống như những trái vả đầu mùa. Giỏ kia có những trái vả rất xấu. Chúng xấu đến nỗi không ai ăn được.

ko.L: 한 바구니에는 처음 익은 무화과 같은 아주 좋은 무화과가 [있었고], 다른 바구니에는 너무 나빠서 먹을 수 없는 아주 나쁜 무화과가 [있었다].
ko.B: 한 바구니에는 맏물 무화과처럼 아주 좋은 무화과가 담겨 있었고, 다른 바구니에는 너무 나빠서 먹을 수 없는 아주 나쁜 무화과가 담겨 있었다.
ko.R: 한 바구니에는 아주 좋은 무화과가 있었다. 그해에 처음 익은 무화과 같았다. 다른 바구니에는 아주 나쁜 무화과가 있었다. 너무 나빠서 아무도 먹을 수 없었다.

pt.L: Um cesto [tinha] figos muito bons, como os figos temporãos; e o outro cesto [tinha] figos muito ruins, que não se podiam comer de tão ruins.
pt.B: Um cesto tinha figos muito bons, como os figos que amadurecem primeiro; o outro cesto tinha figos muito ruins, tão ruins que não se podiam comer.
pt.R: Um cesto tinha figos muito bons, como os primeiros figos da estação. O outro cesto tinha figos muito ruins. Eram tão ruins que ninguém conseguia comê-los.

am.L: አንዱ ቅርጫት እንደ መጀመሪያ ፍሬ በለስ እጅግ መልካም በለስ [ነበረበት]፤ ሌላውም ቅርጫት ከመጥፎነቱ የተነሣ የማይበላ እጅግ መጥፎ በለስ [ነበረበት]።
am.B: አንዱ ቅርጫት ቀድሞ እንደሚበስል በለስ እጅግ መልካም በለስ ይዞ ነበር፤ ሌላው ቅርጫት ደግሞ ከመጥፎነቱ የተነሣ የማይበላ እጅግ መጥፎ በለስ ይዞ ነበር።
am.R: አንዱ ቅርጫት እንደ ወቅቱ የመጀመሪያ በለስ እጅግ ጥሩ በለስ ነበረበት። ሌላው ቅርጫት ደግሞ እጅግ መጥፎ በለስ ነበረበት። በጣም ከመበላሸቱ የተነሣ ማንም ሊበላው አይችልም ነበር።

hi.L: एक टोकरी में बहुत अच्छे अंजीर [थे], पहली उपज के अंजीरों जैसे; और दूसरी टोकरी में बहुत बुरे अंजीर [थे], जो बुरे होने के कारण खाए नहीं जा सकते थे।
hi.B: एक टोकरी में बहुत अच्छे अंजीर थे, जैसे सबसे पहले पकनेवाले अंजीर होते हैं; दूसरी टोकरी में बहुत बुरे अंजीर थे, इतने बुरे कि वे खाए नहीं जा सकते थे।
hi.R: एक टोकरी में बहुत अच्छे अंजीर थे, मौसम के पहले अंजीरों जैसे। दूसरी टोकरी में बहुत बुरे अंजीर थे। वे इतने बुरे थे कि कोई उन्हें खा नहीं सकता था।

ru.L: Одна корзина — смоквы очень хорошие, как смоквы первого урожая; а другая корзина — смоквы очень плохие, которые нельзя было есть из-за [их] негодности.
ru.B: В одной корзине были очень хорошие смоквы, как смоквы, что созревают первыми; в другой корзине были очень плохие смоквы, такие плохие, что их нельзя было есть.
ru.R: В одной корзине был очень хороший инжир, как первый инжир в начале лета. В другой корзине был очень плохой инжир. Он был такой плохой, что никто не мог его есть.

ja.L: 一つのかごには、初なりのいちじくのような、非常に良いいちじくが[あり]、もう一つのかごには、悪くて食べられないほどの、非常に悪いいちじくが[あった]。
ja.B: 一つのかごには、早く熟したいちじくのような、とても良いいちじくが入っていた。もう一つのかごには、とても悪いいちじくが入っていて、あまりに悪くて食べられなかった。
ja.R: 一つのかごには、季節の初めにとれるいちじくのような、とても良いいちじくが入っていました。もう一つのかごには、とても悪いいちじくが入っていました。それはあまりにも悪くて、だれも食べることができませんでした。

uk.L: Один кошик [мав] дуже добрі смокви, як ранні смокви; а другий кошик [мав] дуже погані смокви, яких не можна було їсти через [їхню] поганість.
uk.B: В одному кошику були дуже добрі смокви, як ті, що достигають першими; у другому кошику були дуже погані смокви, такі погані, що їх не можна було їсти.
uk.R: В одному кошику були дуже добрі смокви, як перші смокви в році. У другому кошику були дуже погані смокви. Вони були такі погані, що ніхто не міг їх їсти.

decisions.choice: first-ripe figs: the early figs of early summer, prized as a delicacy
decisions.reason: The first figs ripen on the old wood in early summer, before the main crop. They were sought after and eaten at once (Isaiah 28:4; Hosea 9:10; Micah 7:1).

decisions.choice: which will not be eaten because of badness: too bad to eat
decisions.reason: The phrase returns in verses 3 and 8, and Jeremiah 29:17 takes up the same picture of figs too bad to eat for those left in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the one basket ... the other basket
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "the one basket ... and the one basket" to mean one and the other.

decisions.choice: had / held
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets the basket and its figs side by side without a verb; English supplies one, in brackets at Literal.

decisions.choice: смоквы (L, B); инжир (R)
decisions.reason: The fruit takes the forms settled in Mark and Jeremiah 8: смоквы at Literal and Balanced, инжир at Readable.

decisions.choice: habbakkurot "初なりのいちじく" (L), "早く熟したいちじく" (B), "季節の初めにとれるいちじく" (R).

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to me, what [are] you seeing, Jeremiah? And I said, figs; the figs the good [are] good very, and the bad [are] bad very, which not will be eaten from badness.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "What [are] you seeing, Jeremiah?" And I said, "Figs; the good figs [are] very good, and the bad [are] very bad, which cannot be eaten because of [their] badness."
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} asked me, "What do you see, Jeremiah?" I answered, "Figs. The good figs are very good, and the bad ones are very bad, so bad that they cannot be eaten."
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} asked me, "What do you see, Jeremiah?" I answered, "I see figs. The good ones are very good. But the bad ones are very bad. They are too bad to eat."

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «¿Qué ves, Jeremías?». Y dije: «Higos; los higos buenos, muy buenos, y los malos, muy malos, que no se pueden comer de tan malos».
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me preguntó: «¿Qué ves, Jeremías?». Le respondí: «Higos. Los higos buenos son muy buenos, y los malos son muy malos, tan malos que no se pueden comer».
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me preguntó: «¿Qué ves, Jeremías?». Le respondí: «Veo higos. Los buenos son muy buenos. Pero los malos son muy malos. Están tan malos que no se pueden comer».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me dit : « Que vois-tu, Jérémie ? » Et je dis : « Des figues ; les bonnes figues [sont] très bonnes, et les mauvaises [sont] très mauvaises, au point qu’on ne peut pas les manger tant elles sont mauvaises. »
fr.B: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me demanda : « Que vois-tu, Jérémie ? » Je répondis : « Des figues. Les bonnes figues sont très bonnes, et les mauvaises sont très mauvaises, si mauvaises qu’on ne peut pas les manger. »
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a demandé : « Que vois-tu, Jérémie ? » J’ai répondu : « Je vois des figues. Les bonnes sont très bonnes. Mais les mauvaises sont très mauvaises. Elles sont trop mauvaises pour qu’on les mange. »

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniambia, "Unaona nini, Yeremia?" Nami nikasema, "Tini; tini nzuri [ni] nzuri sana, na mbaya [ni] mbaya sana, zisizoweza kuliwa kwa sababu ya ubaya [wake]."
sw.B: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniuliza, "Unaona nini, Yeremia?" Nikajibu, "Tini. Tini nzuri ni nzuri sana, na zile mbaya ni mbaya sana, mbaya kiasi kwamba haziwezi kuliwa."
sw.R: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniuliza, "Unaona nini, Yeremia?" Nikajibu, "Ninaona tini. Zile nzuri ni nzuri sana. Lakini zile mbaya ni mbaya sana. Ni mbaya mno kuliwa."

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với tôi: "Giê-rê-mi, ngươi thấy gì?" Tôi thưa: "Trái vả; trái vả tốt thì rất tốt, còn trái xấu thì rất xấu, xấu đến nỗi không thể ăn được."
vi.B: Bấy giờ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hỏi tôi: "Giê-rê-mi, con thấy gì?" Tôi thưa: "Trái vả. Những trái vả tốt thì rất tốt, còn những trái xấu thì rất xấu, xấu đến nỗi không ăn được."
vi.R: Bấy giờ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hỏi tôi: "Giê-rê-mi, con thấy gì?" Tôi thưa: "Con thấy trái vả. Những trái tốt thì rất tốt. Còn những trái xấu thì rất xấu. Chúng xấu đến nỗi không ăn được."

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 "예레미야야, 무엇을 보고 있느냐?" 하고 말씀하셨다. 그래서 내가 "무화과입니다. 좋은 무화과는 아주 좋고, 나쁜 것은 아주 나빠서 너무 나빠 먹을 수 없습니다." 하고 말했다.
ko.B: 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 "예레미야야, 무엇이 보이느냐?" 하고 물으셨다. 내가 대답했다. "무화과입니다. 좋은 무화과는 아주 좋고, 나쁜 것은 너무 나빠서 먹을 수가 없습니다."
ko.R: 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 "예레미야야, 무엇이 보이느냐?" 하고 물으셨다. 내가 대답했다. "무화과가 보입니다. 좋은 것은 아주 좋습니다. 그러나 나쁜 것은 아주 나쁩니다. 너무 나빠서 먹을 수가 없습니다."

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me disse: "O que tu [estás] vendo, Jeremias?" E eu disse: "Figos; os figos bons [são] muito bons, e os ruins [são] muito ruins, que não se podem comer de tão ruins."
pt.B: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me perguntou: "O que vês, Jeremias?" Eu respondi: "Figos. Os figos bons são muito bons, e os ruins são muito ruins, tão ruins que não se podem comer."
pt.R: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me perguntou: "O que estás vendo, Jeremias?" Eu respondi: "Vejo figos. Os bons são muito bons. Mas os ruins são muito ruins. São tão ruins que não dá para comer."

am.L: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}ም፦ «ኤርምያስ ሆይ፣ ምን ታያለህ?» አለኝ። እኔም፦ «በለስ፤ መልካሙ በለስ እጅግ መልካም ነው፤ መጥፎውም እጅግ መጥፎ ነው፤ ከመጥፎነቱ የተነሣ አይበላም» አልኩ።
am.B: ከዚያም {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}፦ «ኤርምያስ ሆይ፣ ምን ታያለህ?» ብሎ ጠየቀኝ። እኔም፦ «በለስ። መልካሙ በለስ እጅግ መልካም ነው፤ መጥፎው ደግሞ እጅግ መጥፎ ነው፤ ከመጥፎነቱ የተነሣ ሊበላ አይችልም» ብዬ መለስኩ።
am.R: ከዚያም {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}፦ «ኤርምያስ ሆይ፣ ምን ታያለህ?» ብሎ ጠየቀኝ። እኔም፦ «በለስ አያለሁ። ጥሩዎቹ በጣም ጥሩ ናቸው። መጥፎዎቹ ግን በጣም መጥፎ ናቸው። ለመብላት እንኳ አይሆኑም» ብዬ መለስኩ።

hi.L: और {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने मुझसे कहा, "यिर्मयाह, तुम क्या देख रहे हो?" और मैंने कहा, "अंजीर; अच्छे अंजीर बहुत अच्छे [हैं], और बुरे बहुत बुरे [हैं], जो बुरे होने के कारण खाए नहीं जा सकते।"

hi.R: तब {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने मुझसे पूछा, "यिर्मयाह, तुम क्या देख रहे हो?" मैंने उत्तर दिया, "मुझे अंजीर दिखाई दे रहे हैं। अच्छे अंजीर बहुत अच्छे हैं। पर बुरे अंजीर बहुत बुरे हैं। वे इतने बुरे हैं कि खाए नहीं जा सकते।"

ru.L: И сказал мне {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}: «Что ты видишь, Иеремия?» И я сказал: «Смоквы; смоквы хорошие — очень хорошие, а плохие — очень плохие, которые нельзя есть из-за [их] негодности.»
ru.B: Тогда {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} спросил меня: «Что ты видишь, Иеремия?» Я ответил: «Смоквы. Хорошие смоквы очень хороши, а плохие очень плохи, такие плохие, что их нельзя есть.»
ru.R: Тогда {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} спросил меня: «Что ты видишь, Иеремия?» Я ответил: «Я вижу инжир. Хороший инжир очень хороший. А плохой очень плохой. Он такой плохой, что его нельзя есть.»

ja.L: {{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}はわたしに言われた。「エレミヤよ、あなたは何を見ているか？」わたしは言った。「いちじくです。良いいちじくは非常に良く、悪いものは非常に悪くて、悪さのゆえに食べることができません。」
ja.B: すると、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}はわたしに尋ねられた。「エレミヤよ、何が見えるか？」わたしは答えた。「いちじくです。良いいちじくはとても良く、悪いものはとても悪くて、食べられないほどです。」
ja.R: すると、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}はわたしに尋ねられました。「エレミヤよ、何が見えるか？」わたしは答えました。「いちじくが見えます。良いものはとても良いです。でも、悪いものはとても悪いです。悪すぎて食べられません。」

uk.L: І {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}} сказав мені: «Що ти бачиш, Єреміє?» І я сказав: «Смокви; добрі смокви дуже добрі, а погані дуже погані, яких не можна їсти через [їхню] поганість».
uk.B: Тоді {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}} запитав мене: «Що ти бачиш, Єреміє?» Я відповів: «Смокви. Добрі смокви дуже добрі, а погані дуже погані, такі погані, що їх не можна їсти».
uk.R: Тоді {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}} запитав мене: «Що ти бачиш, Єреміє?» Я відповів: «Я бачу смокви. Добрі дуже добрі. А погані дуже погані. Вони такі погані, що їх не можна їсти».

decisions.choice: What do you see, Jeremiah?: the question that opens the explanation of a vision
decisions.reason: God asked the same question at Jeremiah's call (1:11, 13) and asks it of Amos (Amos 7:8; 8:2). The prophet names what he sees, and God then gives its meaning.

decisions.choice: good, very good ... bad, very bad: the repetition sharpens the contrast
decisions.reason: Jeremiah repeats each adjective ("the good, good very"), and nothing lies between the two kinds of fig. The contrast prepares for the two groups of people in verses 5-10.

decisions.choice: asked; answered; Readable: I see figs
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "asked" for the verb "said" that introduces a question, and "answered" for Jeremiah's reply.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah answers with "thưa"
decisions.reason: Jeremiah answers God, so Vietnamese uses the respectful "thưa"; in Readable he calls himself "con" when he speaks to God, as in his prayers.

decisions.choice: God asks in 해라체; Jeremiah answers in 합쇼체 ("무화과입니다")
decisions.reason: As the terms note: God speaks 해라체, and the prophet speaks to God in 합쇼체.

decisions.choice: तुम when God speaks to Jeremiah
decisions.reason: As in the earlier books, God addressing a person says तुम; तू is kept for people speaking to God. The same holds through this block.

decisions.choice: God's question in the words of 1:11 ("エレミヤよ、あなたは何を見ているか" L, "エレミヤよ、何が見えるか" B, R); Jeremiah answers God politely (です・ます) at every level.
decisions.reason: m1: the question that opens a vision; JER conventions for Jeremiah to God in prose.

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh, God of Israel: like the figs the good the these, so I will regard [the] exile of Judah whom I sent from the place the this [to the] land of [the] Chaldeans for good.

en.L: "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: Like these good figs, so I will regard the exiles of Judah, whom I sent away from this place [to the] land of [the] Chaldeans, for [their] good.
en.B: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this: Like these good figs, so I will regard with favor the exiles from Judah, whom I sent away from this place to the land of the Chaldeans.
en.R: "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says: The people of Judah who were taken away as captives are like these good figs. I sent them away from this place to the land of the Babylonians. But I will look on them with favor.

es.L: «Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel: Como a estos higos buenos, así miraré a los cautivos de Judá, a quienes envié de este lugar a la tierra de los caldeos, para [su] bien.
es.B: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel, dice esto: Como a estos higos buenos, así miraré con favor a los cautivos de Judá, a quienes envié de este lugar a la tierra de los caldeos.
es.R: «Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel: La gente de Judá que fue llevada prisionera es como estos higos buenos. Yo los envié de este lugar a la tierra de los babilonios. Pero los miraré con favor.

fr.L: « Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël : Comme ces bonnes figues, ainsi je regarderai les exilés de Juda, que j’ai envoyés de ce lieu [au] pays des Chaldéens, pour [leur] bien.
fr.B: « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël, dit ceci : Comme on regarde ces bonnes figues, ainsi je regarderai avec bienveillance les exilés de Juda, que j’ai envoyés de ce lieu au pays des Chaldéens.
fr.R: « Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël : Les gens de Juda qu’on a emmenés comme prisonniers sont comme ces bonnes figues. Je les ai envoyés loin de ce lieu, dans le pays des Babyloniens. Mais je les regarderai avec bienveillance.

sw.L: "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, asema hivi: Kama tini hizi nzuri, ndivyo nitakavyowaangalia mateka wa Yuda, niliowapeleka kutoka mahali hapa [mpaka] nchi ya Wakaldayo, kwa mema.
sw.B: "Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, asemavyo: Kama tini hizi nzuri, ndivyo nitakavyowaangalia kwa upendeleo mateka wa Yuda, niliowapeleka kutoka mahali hapa mpaka nchi ya Wakaldayo.
sw.R: "Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, analosema: Watu wa Yuda waliochukuliwa mateka ni kama tini hizi nzuri. Niliwapeleka kutoka mahali hapa mpaka nchi ya Wababeli. Lakini nitawaangalia kwa wema.

vi.L: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán thế này: Như những trái vả tốt này, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sẽ đoái xem những người Giu-đa bị lưu đày, mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã sai đi khỏi nơi này [đến] xứ [của] người Canh-đê, để [làm] điều tốt [cho họ].
vi.B: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán như vầy: Như những trái vả tốt này, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đoái thương những người Giu-đa bị lưu đày, là những người {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã sai đi khỏi nơi này đến xứ của người Canh-đê.
vi.R: "Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán: Những người Giu-đa bị bắt đi làm tù binh giống như những trái vả tốt này. Ta đã sai họ đi khỏi nơi này đến xứ của người Ba-by-lôn. Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đoái thương họ.

ko.L: "이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 내가 이곳에서 갈대아 사람들의 땅으로 보낸 유다의 포로들을 이 좋은 무화과처럼 좋게 보아 줄 것이다.
ko.B: "이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 내가 이곳에서 갈대아 사람들의 땅으로 보낸 유다의 포로들을 이 좋은 무화과처럼 좋게 여기겠다.
ko.R: "이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 포로로 끌려간 유다 백성은 이 좋은 무화과와 같다. 내가 그들을 이곳에서 바빌로니아 사람들의 땅으로 보냈다. 그러나 나는 그들을 좋게 보아 주겠다.

pt.L: "Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de Israel: Como estes figos bons, assim olharei os exilados de Judá, que enviei deste lugar [para a] terra dos caldeus, para [o seu] bem.
pt.B: "Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de Israel: Como estes figos bons, assim olharei com favor os exilados de Judá, que enviei deste lugar para a terra dos caldeus.
pt.R: "É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de Israel, diz: O povo de Judá que foi levado como prisioneiro é como estes figos bons. Eu os mandei deste lugar para a terra dos babilônios. Mas vou olhar para eles com favor.

am.L: «የእስራኤል አምላክ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እንዲህ ይላል፦ እንደነዚህ መልካም በለሶች፣ እንዲሁ ከዚህ ስፍራ ወደ ከለዳውያን ምድር የሰደድኋቸውን የይሁዳን ምርኮኞች ለመልካም እመለከታቸዋለሁ።
am.B: «የእስራኤል አምላክ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እንዲህ ይላል፦ ከዚህ ስፍራ ወደ ከለዳውያን ምድር የሰደድኋቸውን የይሁዳ ምርኮኞች እንደነዚህ መልካም በለሶች በበጎ ዓይን እመለከታቸዋለሁ።
am.R: «የእስራኤል አምላክ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እንዲህ ይላል፦ ተማርከው የተወሰዱት የይሁዳ ሰዎች እንደነዚህ ጥሩ በለሶች ናቸው። እኔ ከዚህ ስፍራ ወደ ባቢሎናውያን ምድር ሰደድኋቸው። ነገር ግን በበጎ ዓይን እመለከታቸዋለሁ።

hi.L: "{{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, इस्राएल के परमेश्वर, यों कहते हैं: इन अच्छे अंजीरों के समान, वैसे ही मैं यहूदा के बंधुओं को, जिन्हें मैंने इस स्थान से कसदियों के देश में भेज दिया है, भलाई के लिए ध्यान में रखूँगा।
hi.B: "{{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, इस्राएल के परमेश्वर, यह कहते हैं: जैसे ये अच्छे अंजीर हैं, वैसे ही मैं यहूदा के उन बंधुओं पर कृपादृष्टि रखूँगा, जिन्हें मैंने इस स्थान से कसदियों के देश में भेज दिया है।
hi.R: "{{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, इस्राएल के परमेश्वर, यह कहते हैं: यहूदा के जो लोग बंदी बनाकर ले जाए गए हैं, वे इन अच्छे अंजीरों जैसे हैं। मैंने ही उन्हें इस स्थान से बाबुलियों के देश में भेजा। पर मैं उन पर कृपा की दृष्टि रखूँगा।

ru.L: «Так говорит {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}, Бог Израиля: Как эти хорошие смоквы, так {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} отмечу изгнанников Иуды, которых {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} отослал из этого места [в] землю халдеев, ко благу [их].
ru.B: «Так говорит {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}, Бог Израиля: Как на эти хорошие смоквы, так {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} буду благосклонно смотреть на изгнанников Иуды, которых {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} отослал из этого места в землю халдеев.
ru.R: «Вот что говорит {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}, Бог Израиля: Люди Иуды, которых увели в плен, похожи на этот хороший инжир. Я отослал их из этого места в землю вавилонян. Но {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} буду смотреть на них с добром.

ja.L: 「イスラエルの神、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}はこう言われる。これらの良いいちじくのように、わたしは、わたしがこの場所からカルデア人の地へ送り出したユダの捕囚の民を、幸いのために心に留める。
ja.B: 「イスラエルの神、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}はこう言われる。これらの良いいちじくのように、わたしは、わたしがこの場所からカルデア人の地へ送り出したユダの捕囚の民に、好意をもって目を留める。
ja.R: 「イスラエルの神、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}はこう言われる。ユダから捕虜として連れて行かれた人々は、この良いいちじくのようだ。わたしが彼らを、この場所からバビロンの国へ送り出したのだ。しかし、わたしは彼らに好意をもって目を留める。

uk.L: «Так говорить {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}, Бог Ізраїля: Як ці добрі смокви, так {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} зважатиму на вигнанців Юди, яких {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} вислав з цього місця [до] краю халдеїв, на добро.
uk.B: «Так говорить {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}, Бог Ізраїля: Як на ці добрі смокви, так {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} прихильно дивитимуся на вигнанців з Юдеї, яких {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} вислав з цього місця до краю халдеїв.
uk.R: «Ось що каже {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}, Бог Ізраїлю: Люди з Юдеї, яких забрали в полон, подібні до цих добрих смокв. Я вислав їх з цього місця до краю вавилонян. Але {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} дивитимуся на них прихильно.

decisions.choice: I will regard ... for good: I will take notice of them with favor, for their benefit
alternatives: I will regard them as good, that is, as better people
decisions.reason: The verb means to recognize or take notice of someone. "For good" names the purpose of God's attention, as in verse 6, and its opposite is "for harm and not for good" (21:10; 44:27). The figs picture how God will treat each group; the text does not say the exiles were better people than those left behind.

decisions.choice: whom I sent away: the exile was God's own act
decisions.reason: Nebuchadrezzar took them (verse 1), but God says that he himself sent them. Babylon was the instrument of his judgment, and the same God will bring them back (verse 6; 29:4, 10-14).

decisions.choice: the exile of Judah: the exiles as one group
decisions.reason: The noun means "exile" and is used collectively for the whole company of exiles.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD (Literal); The LORD says this (Balanced); This is what the LORD says (Readable); speech opens here
decisions.reason: The book's usual wording for the formula. God's speech runs to the end of verse 10 and is quoted in double quotation marks in this prose account, as in 13:9.

decisions.choice: regard with favor / look on them with favor; Readable: the Babylonians
decisions.reason: "For good" can sound like "for ever" in English, so Balanced and Readable say "with favor"; Literal brackets "[their]" to show the sense. Readable says "Babylonians" for the Chaldeans, as Isaiah does, and puts the comparison first in a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: God speaks of the exiles as "họ"
decisions.reason: These are the people God will favour, so Vietnamese uses the neutral "họ", keeping "chúng" for those under judgment in verses 8-10.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다" (L); "... 이렇게 말씀하신다" (B); "... 하시는 말씀이다" (R), with the honorific, though the formula stands inside God's words to Jeremiah
alternatives: "주가 이와 같이 말한다" (God naming himself plainly)
decisions.reason: One rule for Isaiah, Jeremiah and Ezra: the messenger formula keeps the honorific even where God dictates the message, as published at 1 Kings 21:19, 2 Samuel 7:5 and 1 Chronicles 17:4; God's own words that follow stay in the plain style, without -시- for himself.

decisions.choice: "좋게 보아 주다" for "regard ... for good"
decisions.reason: Korean says "regard with favor" in one verb phrase, so Literal needs no bracketed words for "[their] good".

decisions.choice: "የእስራኤል አምላክ እግዚአብሔር እንዲህ ይላል፦" at every level
decisions.reason: The book's formula "Thus says the LORD" (terms list); Elohim with a possessor is "አምላክ", and Amharic puts the title before the name.

decisions.choice: यों कहते हैं (L); यह कहते हैं (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Thus says the LORD" is यों कहते हैं at Literal and यह कहते हैं at Balanced and Readable, the wording 1-2 Kings already use, with God in the honorific plural. The same holds through this block. The exiles (galut) are बंधुए, and the verb galah बंधुआई में ले जाना, as Jeremiah 1:3 has it.

decisions.choice: कसदी (L, B); बाबुली (R)
decisions.reason: The Chaldeans are कसदी, as 2 Kings 24-25 and 2 Chronicles 36:17 have them; Readable says बाबुली (Babylonians), as the English Readable does and as 2 Kings 25:4 does at R.

decisions.choice: Так говорит ГОСПОДЬ (L, B); Вот что говорит ГОСПОДЬ (R)
decisions.reason: The formula koh amar YHWH in the wording the prophets note sets for each level, used the same way through the whole block.

decisions.choice: халдеи (L, B); вавилоняне (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the people (Kasdim); Literal and Balanced keep "халдеи", Readable says "вавилоняне", as the English Readable says "Babylonians".

decisions.choice: 'akkir … letovah "幸いのために心に留める" (L), "好意をもって目を留める" (B, R).
decisions.reason: m1: take notice of them with favor, for their benefit.

decisions.choice: galut Yehudah "ユダの捕囚の民" (L, B), "ユダから捕虜として連れて行かれた人々" (R); 'erets Kasdim "カルデア人の地" (L, B), "バビロンの国" (R).
decisions.reason: m3: the exiles as one group; R as the English R "the land of the Babylonians".

source.text: וְשַׂמְתִּ֨י עֵינִ֤י עֲלֵיהֶם֙ לְטוֹבָ֔ה וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֖ים עַל־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את וּבְנִיתִים֙ וְלֹ֣א אֶהֱרֹ֔ס וּנְטַעְתִּ֖ים וְלֹ֥א אֶתּֽוֹשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will set my eye on them for good, and I will bring them back to the land the this, and I will build them and not I will tear down, and I will plant them and not I will uproot.

en.L: And I will set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes on them for [their] good, and I will bring them back to this land; and I will build them and not tear [them] down, and I will plant them and not uproot [them].
en.B: I will keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes on them for their good and bring them back to this land. I will build them, not tear them down; I will plant them, not uproot them.
en.R: I will watch over them to do them good, and I will bring them back to this land. I will build them and never tear them down. I will plant them and never uproot them.

es.L: Y pondré {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ojos sobre ellos para [su] bien, y los haré volver a esta tierra; y los edificaré y no [los] derribaré, y los plantaré y no [los] arrancaré.
es.B: Mantendré {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ojos sobre ellos para su bien y los haré volver a esta tierra. Los edificaré y no los derribaré; los plantaré y no los arrancaré.
es.R: Los cuidaré para hacerles bien, y los traeré de vuelta a esta tierra. Los edificaré y nunca los derribaré. Los plantaré y nunca los arrancaré.

fr.L: Et je poserai {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} yeux sur eux pour [leur] bien, et je les ramènerai dans ce pays ; et je les bâtirai et je ne [les] démolirai plus, et je les planterai et je ne [les] arracherai plus.
fr.B: Je garderai {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} yeux sur eux pour leur bien et je les ramènerai dans ce pays. Je les bâtirai et ne les démolirai plus ; je les planterai et ne les arracherai plus.
fr.R: Je veillerai sur eux pour leur faire du bien, et je les ramènerai dans ce pays. Je les bâtirai et je ne les démolirai plus jamais. Je les planterai et je ne les arracherai plus jamais.

sw.L: Nami nitaweka macho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} juu yao kwa mema, nami nitawarudisha katika nchi hii; nami nitawajenga wala sitawabomoa, nami nitawapanda wala sitawang'oa.
sw.B: Nitawaangalia daima kwa ajili ya mema yao na kuwarudisha katika nchi hii. Nitawajenga, sitawabomoa; nitawapanda, sitawang'oa.
sw.R: Nitawalinda ili kuwatendea mema, nami nitawarudisha katika nchi hii. Nitawajenga wala sitawabomoa kamwe. Nitawapanda wala sitawang'oa kamwe.

vi.L: Ta sẽ để mắt {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trên họ để [làm] điều tốt [cho họ], và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đem họ trở về xứ này; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ xây dựng họ và không phá đổ, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ trồng họ và không nhổ đi.
vi.B: Ta sẽ để mắt trông nom họ để làm điều tốt cho họ và đem họ trở về xứ này. Ta sẽ xây dựng họ, chứ không phá đổ; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ trồng họ, chứ không nhổ đi.
vi.R: Ta sẽ trông chừng họ để làm điều tốt cho họ, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đem họ trở về xứ này. Ta sẽ xây dựng họ và không bao giờ phá đổ. Ta sẽ trồng họ và không bao giờ nhổ đi.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 그들에게 좋은 일을 하려고 내 눈을 그들 위에 두고, 그들을 이 땅으로 돌아오게 하겠다. 내가 그들을 세우고 허물지 않으며, 그들을 심고 뽑지 않겠다.
ko.B: 내가 그들이 잘되도록 눈여겨 지켜보고, 그들을 이 땅으로 돌아오게 하겠다. 내가 그들을 세우고 허물지 않겠으며, 그들을 심고 뽑지 않겠다.
ko.R: 내가 그들을 지켜보며 그들에게 좋은 일을 해 주겠다. 내가 그들을 이 땅으로 다시 데려오겠다. 내가 그들을 세우고 다시는 허물지 않겠다. 그들을 심고 다시는 뽑지 않겠다.

pt.L: E porei os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} olhos sobre eles para [o seu] bem, e os farei voltar a esta terra; e os construirei e não [os] derrubarei, e os plantarei e não [os] arrancarei.
pt.B: Manterei os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} olhos sobre eles para o seu bem e os farei voltar a esta terra. Eu os construirei, e não os derrubarei; eu os plantarei, e não os arrancarei.
pt.R: Vou cuidar deles para lhes fazer o bem e vou trazê-los de volta a esta terra. Vou construí-los e nunca derrubá-los. Vou plantá-los e nunca arrancá-los.

am.L: ዓይኔንም ለመልካም በእነርሱ ላይ አደርጋለሁ፤ ወደዚህችም ምድር እመልሳቸዋለሁ፤ እሠራቸዋለሁ እንጂ አላፈርሳቸውም፤ እተክላቸዋለሁ እንጂ አልነቅላቸውም።

ru.L: И {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} обращу {{deity_pronoun:мой|Мой}} взор на них ко благу [их], и возвращу их в эту землю; и построю их, и не разрушу, и насажу их, и не искореню.
ru.B: Я буду заботливо смотреть на них ради их блага и верну их в эту землю. Я построю их и не разрушу, насажу их и не искореню.
ru.R: Я буду смотреть за ними, чтобы делать им добро, и верну их в эту землю. Я построю их и никогда не разрушу. Я посажу их и никогда не вырву с корнем.

ja.L: わたしは彼らの上に、幸いのためにわたしの目を置き、彼らをこの地に帰らせる。わたしは彼らを建てて、打ち倒さず、彼らを植えて、引き抜かない。
ja.B: わたしは彼らの幸いのために彼らに目を注ぎ、彼らをこの地に連れ戻す。わたしは彼らを建てて、打ち倒さない。彼らを植えて、引き抜かない。
ja.R: わたしは彼らを見守り、彼らに良いことをする。そして、彼らをこの地に連れ戻す。わたしは彼らを建てて、決して打ち倒さない。彼らを植えて、決して引き抜かない。

uk.L: І {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} зверну {{deity_pronoun:мої|Мої}} очі на них на добро, і поверну їх до цього краю; і {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} будуватиму їх і не руйнуватиму, і садитиму їх і не викорінюватиму.
uk.B: Я пильнуватиму їх {{deity_pronoun:моїми|Моїми}} очима на їхнє добро і поверну їх до цього краю. Я будуватиму їх, а не руйнуватиму; {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} садитиму їх, а не викорінюватиму.
uk.R: Я пильнуватиму їх, щоб робити їм добро, і поверну їх до цього краю. Я будуватиму їх і ніколи не руйнуватиму. Я садитиму їх і ніколи не викорінюватиму.

decisions.choice: set my eye on them for good: watch over them with care, to do them good
decisions.reason: To set one's eye on someone is to give them close attention, and the purpose decides whether it is care or threat (40:4; 39:12). Amos 9:4 has the reverse: "I will set my eye on them for harm and not for good."

decisions.choice: build, tear down, plant, uproot: the four verbs of Jeremiah's call
decisions.reason: These are words of the commission in 1:10, where Jeremiah is set over nations "to uproot and to tear down ... to build and to plant". They return in 18:7-9, 31:28, 42:10 and 45:4. Here only the building and planting are promised, and the tearing down and uprooting are ruled out.

decisions.choice: build them, plant them: the people pictured as a house and a vineyard
decisions.reason: God speaks of the people as something he builds and plants: a family and nation restored and settled in its land for good (compare Exodus 15:17; Amos 9:15).

decisions.choice: build, tear down, plant, uproot
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the verbs as worded at 1:10, so that a reader can hear the call echoed.

decisions.choice: watch over them to do them good
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom of setting one's eyes on someone.

decisions.choice: edificar, derribar, plantar, arrancar
decisions.reason: The verbs of Jeremiah's call keep the Spanish words used in 18:7-9 at every level.

decisions.choice: kujenga, kubomoa, kupanda, kung'oa
decisions.reason: The verbs of Jeremiah's call (1:10) as used in 18:7-9 of this block, so the echo is heard at every level.

decisions.choice: "bâtir, démolir, planter, arracher"
decisions.reason: The verbs of Jeremiah's call as in 18:7-9, so that the echo can be heard.

decisions.choice: "xây dựng ... phá đổ ... trồng ... nhổ đi"
decisions.reason: The verbs of Jeremiah's call, worded as in 18:7-9 so that the echo of 1:10 is heard.

decisions.choice: "세우다, 허물다, 심다, 뽑다"
decisions.reason: The same Korean verbs as in 18:7-9, so the echo of Jeremiah's call (1:10) is heard (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: construir, derrubar, plantar, arrancar
decisions.reason: The verbs of Jeremiah's call keep the Portuguese words 1:10 sets for the whole book, at every level, so that the reader hears the call echoed (m2).

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Hindi
decisions.reason: The English marks God's pronouns ("my") with the deity_pronoun setting. Devanagari has no capital letters, so the Hindi has no such spans; respect for God is carried by the honorific third person (वे, उनका). This holds for every record of this file.

decisions.choice: बनाना, गिराना, रोपना, उखाड़ना
alternatives: निर्माण करना, गिराना, लगाना, उखाड़ फेंकना
decisions.reason: The verbs of Jeremiah's call (1:10) keep the Hindi of 1:10 in this translation at every level (उखाड़ना natash, ढाना natats, नाश करना abad, गिराना haras, बनाना, रोपना), so that the echo can be heard here (build / not overthrow, plant / not uproot) and at 31:28 and 31:40.

decisions.choice: построю, разрушу, насажу, искореню (L, B); построю, разрушу, посажу, вырву с корнем (R)
decisions.reason: The four verbs echo Jeremiah's call (1:10) and keep the words used there at each level.

decisions.choice: The call verbs of 1:10 (m2): banah "建てる", haras "打ち倒す", nata' "植える", natash "引き抜く", at every level.
decisions.reason: JER conventions for the six verbs of the call.

records.literal_gloss: And I will give to them a heart to know me, that I [am] Yahweh; and they will be to me for a people, and I will be to them for God; for they will return to me with all their heart.

en.L: And I will give them a heart to know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and they will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and I will be their God, for they will return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with their whole heart.
en.B: I will give them a heart to know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, to know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and they will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and I will be their God, because they will turn back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with their whole heart.
en.R: I will give them hearts that can know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and understand that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and I will be their God, because they will come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with all their hearts.

es.L: Y les daré un corazón para conocerme, que yo [soy] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}; y serán {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, y yo seré su Dios, porque se volverán a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} de todo su corazón.
es.B: Les daré un corazón para que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} conozcan, para que sepan que yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}; y ellos serán {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, y yo seré su Dios, porque se volverán a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} de todo corazón.
es.R: Les daré un corazón capaz de conocerme y de entender que yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Ellos serán {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, y yo seré su Dios, porque volverán a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} con todo su corazón.

fr.B: Je leur donnerai un cœur capable de {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} connaître, de savoir que je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; ils seront {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple, et je serai leur Dieu, car ils reviendront à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} de tout leur cœur.
fr.R: Je leur donnerai un cœur qui pourra {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} connaître et comprendre que je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Ils seront {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple, et je serai leur Dieu, car ils reviendront à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} de tout leur cœur.

pt.B: Eu lhes darei um coração para {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} conhecer, para saber que eu sou {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}; e eles serão o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo, e eu serei o Deus deles, porque eles se voltarão para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} de todo o coração.
