ru.L: И дам им сердце, чтобы знать {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}}, что {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} — {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}; и будут они {{deity_pronoun:мне|Мне}} народом, а {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} буду им Богом, потому что они вернутся ко {{deity_pronoun:мне|Мне}} всем своим сердцем.
ru.B: Я дам им сердце, чтобы знать {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}}, знать, что {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} — {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}. Они будут {{deity_pronoun:моим|Моим}} народом, а {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} буду их Богом, потому что они вернутся ко {{deity_pronoun:мне|Мне}} всем сердцем.
ru.R: Я дам им сердца, которые смогут знать {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}} и понимать, что {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} — {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}. Они будут {{deity_pronoun:моим|Моим}} народом, а {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} буду их Богом, потому что они вернутся ко {{deity_pronoun:мне|Мне}} всем сердцем.

ja.L: わたしは彼らに、わたしを知る心、わたしが{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}であることを[知る心]を与える。彼らはわたしの民となり、わたしは彼らの神となる。彼らが心を尽くしてわたしに立ち帰るからである。
ja.B: わたしは彼らに、わたしを知る心、わたしが{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}であることを知る心を与える。彼らはわたしの民となり、わたしは彼らの神となる。彼らが心を尽くして、わたしに立ち帰るからだ。
ja.R: わたしは彼らに、わたしを知り、わたしが{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}であることを悟る心を与える。彼らはわたしの民となり、わたしは彼らの神となる。彼らが心から、わたしのもとに戻って来るからだ。

uk.L: І {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} дам їм серце, щоб знати {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}}, що {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}; і вони будуть {{deity_pronoun:моїм|Моїм}} народом, а {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} буду їхнім Богом, бо вони повернуться до {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}} всім своїм серцем.
uk.B: Я дам їм серце, щоб вони знали {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}}, знали, що {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}; і вони будуть {{deity_pronoun:моїм|Моїм}} народом, а {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} буду їхнім Богом, бо вони навернуться до {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}} всім своїм серцем.
uk.R: Я дам їм серця, які зможуть знати {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}} і розуміти, що {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}. Вони будуть {{deity_pronoun:моїм|Моїм}} народом, а {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} буду їхнім Богом, бо вони повернуться до {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}} всім серцем.

decisions.choice: a heart to know me: the inner power and will to know God
decisions.reason: The heart is the inner person: mind, will and desire. Moses told Israel that the LORD had not yet given them "a heart to know" (Deuteronomy 29:3). Here God promises to give it.

decisions.choice: to know that I am the LORD: to know God in a living, faithful relationship
decisions.reason: Knowing God in Jeremiah means more than knowing facts about him; it means doing justice and keeping faith with him (9:23; 22:16). The new covenant promises that all will know him (31:34).

decisions.choice: they will be my people, and I will be their God: the covenant promise
decisions.reason: These words sum up the covenant (Exodus 6:7; Leviticus 26:12). Jeremiah uses them in 7:23 and 11:4 and in the promises of restoration (30:22; 31:33; 32:38).

decisions.choice: for they will return: the return comes from the new heart God gives
decisions.reason: The word can mean "for" or "when". Since the gift of the heart comes first in the verse, their wholehearted return is its result and the sign of the renewed covenant (compare 29:13).

decisions.choice: They will be my people, and I will be their God
alternatives: they will be to me a people, and I will be to them God
decisions.reason: The covenant promise is worded as in 7:23 and 11:4.

decisions.choice: hearts that can know me and understand
decisions.reason: Readable says "hearts" for the many people and adds "understand" to make the two parts of the phrase clear.

decisions.choice: serán mi pueblo, y yo seré su Dios
decisions.reason: The covenant promise keeps this Spanish wording each time it returns (30:22; 31:33; 32:38).

decisions.choice: se volverán a mí
decisions.reason: *Shuv* of turning to God is "volver(se)", never "arrepentirse", as the terms note sets for Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: watanirudia
decisions.reason: *Shuv* of repentance is "kunirudia" at every level, as the terms note sets, so turning back to God and returning home are heard as one word.

decisions.choice: "ils seront mon peuple, et je serai leur Dieu"; "reviendront"
alternatives: ils seront pour moi un peuple
decisions.reason: The covenant promise in the words Hebrews 8:10 uses in French for the same promise, and "revenir" as set for shuv in Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: "họ sẽ là dân của Ta, và Ta sẽ là Đức Chúa Trời của họ"
decisions.reason: The covenant promise is worded at every level as the terms note settles for 31:33 (after Hebrews 8:10), so the same words are heard each time it returns (30:22; 31:1; 32:38).

decisions.choice: "quay về cùng Ta" (L, B); "ăn năn quay về" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's wording for "shuv" as repentance; "trở về" is kept for coming home from exile, as in verse 6.

decisions.choice: "그들은 내 백성이 되고, 나는 그들의 하나님이 될 것이다"
alternatives: "그들은 내 백성이 되겠고 나는 그들의 하나님이 되리라"
decisions.reason: The covenant promise in the wording the terms note sets for Jeremiah, so 24:7, 30:22 and 31:33 match; the archaic ending is avoided.

decisions.choice: "돌아오다" for *shuv*
decisions.reason: The terms note's word for returning to God in Jeremiah; "회개하다" stays for the Greek.

decisions.choice: Covenant formula: "እነርሱም ሕዝብ ይሆኑኛል፤ እኔም አምላክ እሆናቸዋለሁ" (Literal), "እነርሱ ሕዝቤ ይሆናሉ፤ እኔም አምላካቸው እሆናለሁ" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The phrases are those of the Amharic Hebrews 8:10, which quotes the formula from Jeremiah 31:33; the same wording is kept wherever Jeremiah repeats it (30:22; 31:1, 33), in the Hebrew order (people first, then God).

decisions.choice: वे मेरी प्रजा होंगे, और मैं उनका परमेश्वर होऊँगा (L, B); मेरे लोग (R)
decisions.reason: The covenant promise has one wording through this block (here, 30:22, 31:1, 31:33). The second half matches Hebrews 8:10 ("मैं उनका परमेश्वर होऊँगा"); God's "my people" is मेरी प्रजा at L and B as in Isaiah, मेरे लोग at R, as Hebrews 8:10 has it.

decisions.choice: будут они мне народом, а я буду им Богом (L); будут моим народом, а я буду их Богом (B, R)
decisions.reason: The covenant promise is worded the same way wherever it recurs in this block (30:22; 31:1, 33), as the English does.

decisions.choice: The covenant formula in the Hebrew order of this verse: "彼らはわたしの民となり、わたしは彼らの神となる" (every level), as 7:23 and 11:4.
decisions.reason: JER conventions.

decisions.choice: yashuvu "立ち帰る" (L, B), "戻って来る" (R).
decisions.reason: The JER shuv pair.

source.text: וְכַתְּאֵנִים֙ הָֽרָע֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־תֵאָכַ֖לְנָה מֵרֹ֑עַ כִּי־כֹ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה כֵּ֣ן אֶ֠תֵּן אֶת־צִדְקִיָּ֨הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֤ה וְאֶת־שָׂרָיו֙ וְאֵ֣ת׀שְׁאֵרִ֣ית יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם הַנִּשְׁאָרִים֙ בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את וְהַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And like the figs the bad which not will be eaten from badness, for thus says Yahweh, so I will give Zedekiah king of Judah, and his princes, and [the] remnant of Jerusalem the remaining in the land the this, and the dwelling in [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: And like the bad figs, which cannot be eaten because of [their] badness, indeed, thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, so I will treat Zedekiah king of Judah, and his princes, and the remnant of Jerusalem who remain in this land, and those who live in the land of Egypt.
en.B: But as for the bad figs, so bad that they cannot be eaten, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: In the same way I will treat Zedekiah king of Judah, his officials, the rest of Jerusalem who are left in this land, and those who are living in the land of Egypt.
en.R: But the bad figs are so bad that no one can eat them. And this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I will treat Zedekiah king of Judah like those bad figs. I will do the same to his leaders, to the rest of the people of Jerusalem who are still in this land, and to those who are living in Egypt.

es.L: Y como los higos malos, que no se pueden comer de tan malos, así, ciertamente, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, trataré a Sedequías, rey de Judá, y a sus príncipes, y al remanente de Jerusalén que queda en esta tierra, y a los que habitan en la tierra de Egipto.
es.B: Pero en cuanto a los higos malos, tan malos que no se pueden comer, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: De la misma manera trataré a Sedequías, rey de Judá, a sus jefes, al resto de Jerusalén que queda en esta tierra y a los que viven en la tierra de Egipto.
es.R: Pero los higos malos son tan malos que nadie se los puede comer. Y esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Trataré a Sedequías, rey de Judá, como a esos higos malos. Lo mismo haré con sus dirigentes, con el resto de la gente de Jerusalén que sigue en esta tierra y con los que viven en Egipto.

fr.L: Et comme les mauvaises figues, qu’on ne peut pas manger tant elles sont mauvaises, oui, ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, ainsi je traiterai Sédécias, roi de Juda, et ses princes, et le reste de Jérusalem qui demeure dans ce pays, et ceux qui habitent au pays d’Égypte.
fr.B: Mais quant aux mauvaises figues, si mauvaises qu’on ne peut pas les manger, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : C’est ainsi que je traiterai Sédécias, roi de Juda, ses chefs, le reste de Jérusalem qui est resté dans ce pays, et ceux qui habitent au pays d’Égypte.
fr.R: Mais les mauvaises figues sont si mauvaises que personne ne peut les manger. Et voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Je traiterai Sédécias, le roi de Juda, comme ces mauvaises figues. Je ferai la même chose à ses chefs, aux autres habitants de Jérusalem qui sont encore dans ce pays, et à ceux qui habitent en Égypte.

sw.L: Na kama tini mbaya zisizoweza kuliwa kwa sababu ya ubaya [wake], hakika, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi, ndivyo nitakavyomtendea Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda, na wakuu wake, na mabaki ya Yerusalemu waliobaki katika nchi hii, na wale wanaokaa katika nchi ya Misri.
sw.B: Lakini kuhusu tini mbaya, zilizo mbaya kiasi kwamba haziwezi kuliwa, hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Vivyo hivyo nitamtendea Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda, maafisa wake, mabaki ya Yerusalemu walioachwa katika nchi hii, na wale wanaoishi katika nchi ya Misri.
sw.R: Lakini tini mbaya ni mbaya kiasi kwamba hakuna mtu anayeweza kuzila. Na hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Nitamtendea Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda kama tini hizo mbaya. Nitawatendea vivyo hivyo viongozi wake, watu wa Yerusalemu waliobaki ambao bado wako katika nchi hii, na wale wanaoishi Misri.

vi.L: Còn như những trái vả xấu không thể ăn được vì quá xấu, thật vậy, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán thế này, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sẽ phó Sê-đê-kia vua Giu-đa, các quan trưởng của vua, những người sót lại của Giê-ru-sa-lem còn ở trong xứ này, và những kẻ đang ở trong xứ Ai Cập như vậy.
vi.B: Nhưng còn những trái vả xấu, xấu đến nỗi không ăn được, thì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán như vầy: Ta cũng sẽ đối xử như thế với Sê-đê-kia vua Giu-đa, các quan chức của vua, những người còn lại của Giê-ru-sa-lem đang ở trong xứ này, và những kẻ đang sống trong xứ Ai Cập.
vi.R: Nhưng những trái vả xấu thì xấu đến nỗi không ai ăn được. Và đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: Ta sẽ đối xử với Sê-đê-kia vua Giu-đa như những trái vả xấu ấy. Ta cũng sẽ làm như vậy với các nhà lãnh đạo của vua, với những người dân Giê-ru-sa-lem còn ở lại trong xứ này, và với những kẻ đang sống ở Ai Cập.

ko.L: 그리고 너무 나빠서 먹을 수 없는 나쁜 무화과처럼, 참으로 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다, 내가 유다 왕 시드기야와 그의 고관들과 이 땅에 남아 있는 예루살렘의 남은 자들과 이집트 땅에 사는 자들을 그렇게 만들겠다.
ko.B: 그러나 너무 나빠서 먹을 수 없는 나쁜 무화과에 대하여 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 내가 유다 왕 시드기야와 그의 관리들과 이 땅에 남아 있는 예루살렘의 나머지 사람들과 이집트 땅에 사는 사람들을 그 무화과처럼 대하겠다.
ko.R: 나쁜 무화과는 너무 나빠서 아무도 먹을 수 없다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 내가 유다 왕 시드기야를 그 나쁜 무화과처럼 대하겠다. 그의 지도자들과, 아직 이 땅에 남아 있는 예루살렘의 나머지 사람들과, 이집트에 가서 사는 사람들에게도 그렇게 하겠다.

pt.L: E como os figos ruins, que não se podem comer de tão ruins, sim, assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, assim tratarei Zedequias, rei de Judá, e os seus príncipes, e o remanescente de Jerusalém que ficou nesta terra, e os que moram na terra do Egito.
pt.B: Mas quanto aos figos ruins, tão ruins que não se podem comer, assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: Do mesmo modo tratarei Zedequias, rei de Judá, os seus oficiais, o resto de Jerusalém que ficou nesta terra e os que estão morando na terra do Egito.
pt.R: Mas os figos ruins são tão ruins que ninguém consegue comê-los. E é isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} diz: Vou tratar Zedequias, rei de Judá, como esses figos ruins. Vou fazer o mesmo com os seus líderes, com o resto do povo de Jerusalém que ainda está nesta terra e com os que estão morando no Egito.

am.L: ከመጥፎነታቸውም የተነሣ እንደማይበሉት እንደ መጥፎዎቹ በለሶች፣ በእርግጥ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እንዲህ ይላል፣ እንዲሁ የይሁዳን ንጉሥ ሴዴቅያስን፣ አለቆቹንም፣ በዚህች ምድር የቀሩትን የኢየሩሳሌምን ቅሬታ፣ በግብፅ ምድር የሚኖሩትንም አደርጋቸዋለሁ።
am.B: ከመጥፎነታቸው የተነሣ ስለማይበሉት መጥፎ በለሶች ግን {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እንዲህ ይላል፦ የይሁዳን ንጉሥ ሴዴቅያስን፣ ባለ ሥልጣናቱን፣ በዚህች ምድር የቀሩትን የኢየሩሳሌም ሰዎችና በግብፅ ምድር የሚኖሩትን እንዲሁ አደርጋቸዋለሁ።
am.R: መጥፎዎቹ በለሶች ግን በጣም መጥፎ ስለ ሆኑ ማንም ሊበላቸው አይችልም። {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}ም እንዲህ ይላል፦ የይሁዳን ንጉሥ ሴዴቅያስን እንደነዚያ መጥፎ በለሶች አደርገዋለሁ። መሪዎቹን፣ በዚህች ምድር የቀሩትን የኢየሩሳሌም ሰዎችና በግብፅ የሚኖሩትንም እንዲሁ አደርጋቸዋለሁ።

hi.L: और उन बुरे अंजीरों के समान, जो बुरे होने के कारण खाए नहीं जा सकते, हाँ, {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} यों कहते हैं, वैसे ही मैं यहूदा के राजा सिदकिय्याह को, और उसके हाकिमों को, और यरूशलेम के बचे हुए लोगों को जो इस देश में रह गए हैं, और उन्हें जो मिस्र देश में रहते हैं, कर दूँगा।
hi.B: पर उन बुरे अंजीरों के विषय में, जो इतने बुरे हैं कि खाए नहीं जा सकते, {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} यह कहते हैं: वैसा ही मैं यहूदा के राजा सिदकिय्याह के साथ, उसके अधिकारियों के साथ, यरूशलेम के बाक़ी लोगों के साथ जो इस देश में बचे हैं, और उनके साथ जो मिस्र देश में रह रहे हैं, व्यवहार करूँगा।
hi.R: पर बुरे अंजीर इतने बुरे हैं कि कोई उन्हें खा नहीं सकता। और {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} यह कहते हैं: मैं यहूदा के राजा सिदकिय्याह के साथ उन बुरे अंजीरों जैसा व्यवहार करूँगा। मैं उसके अगुवों के साथ, यरूशलेम के उन बाक़ी लोगों के साथ जो अब भी इस देश में हैं, और उनके साथ जो मिस्र में रह रहे हैं, ऐसा ही करूँगा।

ru.L: И как плохие смоквы, которые нельзя есть из-за [их] негодности, — ведь так говорит {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}, — так {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} поступлю с Седекией, царём Иудейским, и с его князьями, и с остатком Иерусалима, оставшимся в этой земле, и с живущими в земле Египта.
ru.B: А что до плохих смокв, таких плохих, что их нельзя есть, то так говорит {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}: так же {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} поступлю с Седекией, царём Иуды, с его вельможами, с остатком Иерусалима, оставшимся в этой земле, и с теми, кто живёт в земле Египта.
ru.R: Плохой инжир такой плохой, что его никто не может есть. И вот что говорит {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}: Я поступлю с Седекией, царём Иуды, как с этим плохим инжиром. Так же {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} поступлю с его начальниками, с остальными жителями Иерусалима, которые ещё остались в этой земле, и с теми, кто живёт в Египте.

ja.L: また、悪くて食べられないほどの悪いいちじくのように――まことに、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}はこう言われる――、わたしはユダの王ツィドキヤと、その長たちと、この地に残っているエルサレムの残りの者と、エジプトの地に住んでいる者たちを、そのようにする。
ja.B: しかし、あまりに悪くて食べられない悪いいちじくについて、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}はこう言われる。わたしは、ユダの王ツィドキヤと、その高官たちと、この地に残っているエルサレムの残りの者と、エジプトの地に住んでいる者たちを、同じように扱う。
ja.R: しかし、悪いいちじくは、あまりにも悪くて、だれも食べられない。{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}はこう言われる。わたしは、ユダの王ツィドキヤを、あの悪いいちじくのように扱う。彼の指導者たちにも、この地にまだ残っているエルサレムの人々にも、エジプトに住んでいる人々にも、同じようにする。

uk.L: А як ті погані смокви, яких не можна їсти через [їхню] поганість, справді, так говорить {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}, так {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} вчиню з Седекією, царем Юдеї, і з його князями, і з рештою Єрусалима, що залишилися в цьому краї, і з тими, хто живе в краї Єгипту.
uk.B: А щодо поганих смокв, таких поганих, що їх не можна їсти, то так говорить {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}: Так само {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} вчиню з Седекією, царем Юдеї, з його урядниками, з рештою Єрусалима, що залишилися в цьому краї, і з тими, хто живе в краї Єгипту.
uk.R: Але погані смокви такі погані, що ніхто не може їх їсти. І ось що каже {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}: Я вчиню з Седекією, царем Юдеї, як із тими поганими смоквами. Те саме {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} зроблю з його провідниками, з рештою людей Єрусалима, які ще залишилися в цьому краї, і з тими, хто живе в Єгипті.

decisions.choice: for thus says the LORD: the formula breaks into the comparison for emphasis
decisions.reason: The sentence begins the comparison ("like the bad figs"), stops to restate that the LORD is speaking, and then completes it ("so I will ..."). The interruption stresses the seriousness of what follows.

decisions.choice: so I will give: so I will treat them, make them like the bad figs
alternatives: so I will hand them over (to their enemies)
decisions.reason: The verb "give" here means to make or treat someone in a certain way, as in verse 9 ("I will make them a horror"). The thought of handing them over is close, since 21:7 says Zedekiah will be given into Nebuchadrezzar's hand.

decisions.choice: the remnant of Jerusalem who remain in this land: those not taken in 597 BC
decisions.reason: Those left behind with Zedekiah could think that they were the favored ones and the exiles the rejected (compare Ezekiel 11:15; 33:24). The vision turns that view upside down.

decisions.choice: those who live in the land of Egypt: Judeans who had already gone to Egypt
decisions.reason: The text does not say who they were. Some may have gone with King Jehoahaz when Pharaoh took him there (2 Kings 23:34), others as refugees or soldiers. Chapters 42-44 tell of a later and larger flight to Egypt and of God's word against it.

decisions.choice: princes (Literal), officials (Balanced), leaders (Readable); remnant (Literal), the rest (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The usual wording for princes in these books. "Remnant" means the people left over; Balanced and Readable say "the rest".

decisions.choice: the comparison made a sentence of its own; Readable repeats "like those bad figs"
decisions.reason: English cannot easily hold the comparison open across the interrupting formula, so Balanced and Readable close it first and then give the LORD's words. Readable repeats the picture so the comparison stays clear.

decisions.choice: बचे हुए लोग (L); बाक़ी लोग (B, R)
decisions.reason: The remnant is बचे हुए लोग at L, as the terms note sets it; here the sense is simply "the rest" of Jerusalem's people, so Balanced and Readable say बाक़ी लोग, as the English says "the rest".

decisions.choice: остаток (L, B); остальные жители (R)
decisions.reason: The remnant takes the prophets note's word "остаток"; Readable says who they are, as the English Readable says "the rest of the people".

decisions.choice: ki koh 'amar YHWH set between dashes at L, breaking into the comparison as in the Hebrew (m1).
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the interruption; B and R make the comparison a sentence of its own, as the English.

decisions.choice: Tsidqiyyahu "ツィドキヤ" (2 Kings and JER form); sarav "その長たち" (L), "高官たち" (B), "指導者たち" (R); she'erit "残りの者" (L, B), "残っている…人々" (R).
decisions.reason: JER and prophetic conventions.

source.text: וּנְתַתִּים֙ לְזַעֲוָ֣ה לְרָעָ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֑רֶץ לְחֶרְפָּ֤ה וּלְמָשָׁל֙ לִשְׁנִינָ֣ה וְלִקְלָלָ֔ה בְּכָל־הַמְּקֹמ֖וֹת אֲשֶֽׁר־אַדִּיחֵ֥ם שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will give them for a horror, for evil, to all [the] kingdoms of the earth, for a reproach and for a proverb, for a byword and for a curse, in all the places where I will drive them there.

en.L: And I will make them a horror, a disaster, to all the kingdoms of the earth, a reproach and a proverb, a byword and a curse, in all the places where I will drive them.
en.B: I will make them a horror and a disaster to all the kingdoms of the earth. In all the places where I drive them, they will be a disgrace and a proverb, a byword and a curse.
en.R: All the kingdoms of the earth will be horrified at the disaster that comes on them. In all the places where I drive them, people will insult them and tell stories about them. They will make fun of them and use their name as a curse.

es.L: Y los haré un horror, un mal, para todos los reinos de la tierra, oprobio y refrán, burla y maldición, en todos los lugares adonde los arroje.
es.B: Haré de ellos un horror y una desgracia para todos los reinos de la tierra. En todos los lugares adonde los arroje, serán una vergüenza y un refrán, objeto de burla y de maldición.
es.R: Todos los reinos de la tierra se horrorizarán por la desgracia que les vendrá. En todos los lugares adonde los arroje, la gente los insultará y contará historias sobre ellos. Se burlarán de ellos y usarán su nombre para maldecir.

fr.L: Et je ferai d’eux une horreur, un malheur, pour tous les royaumes de la terre, un opprobre et un proverbe, un sujet de moquerie et une malédiction, dans tous les lieux où je les chasserai.
fr.B: Je ferai d’eux un objet d’horreur et de malheur pour tous les royaumes de la terre. Dans tous les lieux où je les chasserai, ils seront un objet de honte et un proverbe, un sujet de moquerie et un nom qu’on utilise pour maudire.
fr.R: Tous les royaumes de la terre seront horrifiés par le malheur qui leur arrivera. Dans tous les lieux où je les chasserai, les gens les insulteront et raconteront des histoires sur eux. Ils se moqueront d’eux et se serviront de leur nom pour maudire.

sw.L: Nami nitawafanya kuwa kitisho, maafa, kwa falme zote za dunia, aibu na mithali, dhihaka na laana, katika mahali pote nitakapowafukuzia.
sw.B: Nitawafanya kuwa kitisho na maafa kwa falme zote za dunia. Katika mahali pote nitakapowafukuzia, watakuwa aibu na mithali, kitu cha kudhihakiwa na laana.
sw.R: Falme zote za dunia zitaogopa kwa sababu ya maafa yatakayowapata. Katika mahali pote nitakapowafukuzia, watu watawatukana na kutunga hadithi kuwahusu. Watawadhihaki na kulitumia jina lao kama laana.

vi.L: Ta sẽ làm cho chúng thành một điều kinh hoàng, một tai họa, cho mọi vương quốc trên đất, một sự sỉ nhục và một câu tục ngữ, một lời chế giễu và một lời rủa sả, tại mọi nơi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ xua đuổi chúng đến.
vi.B: Ta sẽ làm cho chúng thành một điều kinh hoàng và một tai họa cho mọi vương quốc trên đất. Tại mọi nơi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} xua đuổi chúng đến, chúng sẽ thành sự sỉ nhục và câu tục ngữ, đề tài chế giễu và lời nguyền rủa.
vi.R: Mọi vương quốc trên đất sẽ kinh hoàng khi thấy tai họa giáng trên chúng. Tại mọi nơi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} xua đuổi chúng đến, người ta sẽ sỉ nhục chúng và đặt chuyện về chúng. Người ta sẽ chế giễu chúng và dùng tên chúng để nguyền rủa.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 그들을 땅의 모든 나라에 공포와 재앙이 되게 하고, 내가 그들을 쫓아낼 모든 곳에서 치욕과 속담거리와 조롱거리와 저주가 되게 하겠다.
ko.B: 내가 그들을 세상 모든 나라에 공포의 대상, 재앙의 본보기가 되게 하겠다. 내가 그들을 쫓아 보내는 곳마다 그들은 수치와 속담거리, 웃음거리와 저주거리가 될 것이다.
ko.R: 세상 모든 나라가 그들에게 닥친 재앙을 보고 몸서리칠 것이다. 내가 그들을 쫓아 보내는 곳마다 사람들이 그들을 모욕하고 그들 이야기를 하며 비웃을 것이다. 사람들은 저주할 때에 그들의 이름을 쓸 것이다.

pt.L: E farei deles um horror, uma desgraça, para todos os reinos da terra, uma afronta e um provérbio, uma zombaria e uma maldição, em todos os lugares para onde eu os expulsar.
pt.B: Farei deles um objeto de horror e de desgraça para todos os reinos da terra. Em todos os lugares para onde eu os expulsar, eles serão uma vergonha e um provérbio, objeto de zombaria e de maldição.
pt.R: Todos os reinos da terra vão ficar horrorizados com a desgraça que vai cair sobre eles. Em todos os lugares para onde eu os expulsar, as pessoas vão insultá-los e contar histórias sobre eles. Vão zombar deles e usar o nome deles para amaldiçoar.

am.L: ለምድር መንግሥታትም ሁሉ ድንጋጤና ክፉ ነገር አደርጋቸዋለሁ፤ በምሰድዳቸውም ስፍራ ሁሉ ስድብና ምሳሌ፣ መተረቻና እርግማን [ይሆናሉ]።
am.B: ለምድር መንግሥታት ሁሉ የድንጋጤና የጥፋት ምልክት አደርጋቸዋለሁ። በምሰድዳቸው ስፍራ ሁሉ መሰደቢያና ምሳሌ፣ መተረቻና መራገሚያ ይሆናሉ።
am.R: የምድር መንግሥታት ሁሉ በእነርሱ ላይ በሚደርሰው ጥፋት ይደነግጣሉ። በምሰድዳቸው ስፍራ ሁሉ ሰዎች ይሰድቧቸዋል፤ ስለ እነርሱም ተረት ይናገራሉ። ይሳለቁባቸዋል፤ ሲራገሙም ስማቸውን ይጠራሉ።

hi.L: और मैं उन्हें पृथ्वी के सब राज्यों के लिए भय का कारण, विपत्ति, और उन सब स्थानों में जहाँ मैं उन्हें भगा दूँगा, निंदा और कहावत, ताना और शाप बना दूँगा।
hi.B: मैं उन्हें पृथ्वी के सब राज्यों के लिए भय का कारण और विपत्ति का कारण बना दूँगा। जिन जिन स्थानों में मैं उन्हें भगा दूँगा, वहाँ वे अपमान और कहावत, ताने और शाप का विषय बनेंगे।
hi.R: पृथ्वी के सब राज्य उन पर आई विपत्ति को देखकर काँप उठेंगे। जिन जिन स्थानों में मैं उन्हें भगा दूँगा, वहाँ लोग उनका अपमान करेंगे और उनके बारे में किस्से सुनाएँगे। वे उनका मज़ाक़ उड़ाएँगे और शाप देते समय उनका नाम लेंगे।

ru.L: И сделаю их ужасом, бедствием для всех царств земли, позором и притчей, насмешкой и проклятием во всех местах, куда {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} изгоню их.
ru.B: Я сделаю их ужасом и бедствием для всех царств земли. Во всех местах, куда {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} изгоню их, они будут позором и притчей, посмешищем и проклятием.
ru.R: Все царства земли будут в ужасе от беды, которая придёт на них. Во всех местах, куда {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} их прогоню, люди будут оскорблять их и рассказывать о них притчи. Над ними будут смеяться, а их имя будут произносить, когда проклинают.

ja.L: わたしは彼らを、地のすべての王国にとって恐怖とし、災いとする。わたしが彼らを追いやるすべての場所で、そしりとし、ことわざとし、物笑いの種とし、呪いとする。
ja.B: わたしは彼らを、地のすべての王国にとって恐怖の的とし、災いとする。わたしが彼らを追いやるすべての場所で、彼らはそしりとなり、ことわざとなり、物笑いの種となり、呪いの言葉となる。
ja.R: 世界中の国々は、彼らに起こる災いを見て震え上がる。わたしが彼らを追いやるすべての場所で、人々は彼らをののしり、彼らのことを話の種にする。彼らをあざ笑い、のろいの言葉に彼らの名を使う。

uk.L: І {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} зроблю їх жахом, лихом для всіх царств землі, ганьбою і притчею, посміховищем і прокляттям у всіх місцях, куди {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} їх вижену.
uk.B: Я зроблю їх жахом і лихом для всіх царств землі. У всіх місцях, куди {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} їх вижену, вони будуть ганьбою і притчею, посміховищем і прокляттям.
uk.R: Усі царства землі жахнуться від лиха, що спіткає їх. У всіх місцях, куди {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} їх вижену, люди ображатимуть їх і розповідатимуть про них оповідки. Вони глузуватимуть з них і вживатимуть їхнє імʼя як прокляття.

decisions.choice: horror: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) put two letters of this word in a different order; the scribes marked the usual form to be read aloud (qere). Both name the same word.

decisions.choice: a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth: a sight that makes the nations tremble
decisions.reason: The word means something that causes people to shake with fear. The whole phrase comes from the covenant curses in Deuteronomy 28:25, and Jeremiah repeats it in 15:4, 29:18 and 34:17.

decisions.choice: for evil: a disaster, or for harm
alternatives: a copying slip that repeats part of the word before it
decisions.reason: The word means evil, harm or disaster. It may name the disaster the people become, or say that God gives them over "for harm" (compare 21:10). The same phrase in 15:4, 29:18 and 34:17 lacks it, and the two words look alike, so it may have entered by copying; the meaning of the verse is not changed either way.

decisions.choice: a reproach, a proverb, a byword and a curse: the warnings of the covenant fulfilled
decisions.reason: Moses warned that Israel would become "a horror, a proverb and a byword" among the nations (Deuteronomy 28:37), and God told Solomon the same of the temple and people (1 Kings 9:7). The nations will speak of them as an example of disaster and mock them.

decisions.choice: a curse: a name used when people curse
decisions.reason: People will use their fate in curses, as 29:22 shows: "May the LORD make you like Zedekiah and like Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire."

decisions.choice: horror; reproach (Literal) / disgrace (Balanced); proverb, byword, curse; Readable in sentences
decisions.reason: "Proverb" and "byword" follow Deuteronomy 28:37 and 1 Kings 9:7, and "horror" follows Deuteronomy 28:25. Readable says what the nouns mean in sentences of its own, as at Deuteronomy 28:37.

decisions.choice: In all the places where I drive them, first in its sentence
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable divide the verse into two sentences, putting the place of the mockery first in the second.

decisions.choice: aibu, mithali, dhihaka, laana
decisions.reason: The four words of the covenant warnings, each with its own Swahili noun at Literal and Balanced; Readable turns them into what people will do, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "sự rủa sả" (L); "lời nguyền rủa" (B); "dùng tên chúng để nguyền rủa" (R)
decisions.reason: The curse in these lists is the curse of the covenant; Readable says what it means, as meaning decision m5 explains. "Điều kinh hoàng" is the "horror" of 18:16.

decisions.choice: "공포 ... 치욕 ... 속담거리 ... 조롱거리 ... 저주" (L); "공포의 대상 ... 수치 ... 웃음거리 ... 저주거리" (B)
decisions.reason: One wording per level for Jeremiah's lists of horror and curse, as the English; Readable turns the list into sentences, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: um horror, uma afronta, um provérbio, uma zombaria, uma maldição
decisions.reason: The covenant curses that this verse takes up (m2, m4) keep the words Deuteronomy 28:25 and 37 have in Portuguese, "um horror", "um provérbio" and "uma zombaria", so the reader can hear the warning fulfilled; "afronta" (L) and "vergonha" (B) say the scorn heaped on someone, as the English says "reproach" and "disgrace".

decisions.choice: horror "ድንጋጤ"; reproach "ስድብ" / "መሰደቢያ"; proverb "ምሳሌ"; byword "መተረቻ"; curse "እርግማን" / "መራገሚያ"
decisions.reason: Jeremiah repeats this list of the covenant's curses (25:9, 18; 29:18); the same Amharic words are kept each time.

decisions.choice: भय का कारण; निंदा (L) / अपमान (B); कहावत; ताना; शाप
decisions.reason: The covenant curses of Deuteronomy 28:25, 37 are given one Hindi word each, kept through the book (25:9, 18; 29:18; 42:18; 44:12): भय का कारण for the horror (za'avah here, shammah elsewhere), as Deuteronomy 28:25, 37 have it, कहावत for the proverb, ताना for the byword (sheninah, a sharp saying), शाप for the curse.

decisions.choice: притча, насмешка (L); притча, посмешище (B)
decisions.reason: "Proverb" and "byword" are the words of the covenant warnings (Deuteronomy 28:37); Russian "притча" and "посмешище" keep the sense of a name others mock.

decisions.choice: leza'avah "恐怖" (L), "恐怖の的" (B), as 15:4; cherpah "そしり", mashal "ことわざ", sheninah "物笑いの種", qelalah "呪い" (L, B), R in sentences as the English R.
decisions.reason: m2, m4, m5; the JER-3 form for za'avah.

decisions.choice: "In all the places where I will drive them" comes before the list at every level.
decisions.reason: Japanese puts the place phrase before the predicate; the English B and R do the same.

records.literal_gloss: And I will send on them the sword, the famine and the pestilence, until their being finished from on the ground which I gave to them and to their fathers.

en.L: And I will send among them the sword, the famine and the pestilence, until they are finished off from the land that I gave to them and to their fathers."
en.B: I will send sword, famine and plague against them until they are wiped out from the land I gave to them and to their ancestors."
en.R: I will send war, famine and disease against them until they are all gone from the land I gave to them and to their ancestors."

es.L: Y enviaré entre ellos la espada, el hambre y la peste, hasta que sean exterminados de la tierra que les di a ellos y a sus padres».
es.B: Enviaré contra ellos la espada, el hambre y la peste hasta que desaparezcan de la tierra que les di a ellos y a sus antepasados».
es.R: Enviaré contra ellos la guerra, el hambre y las enfermedades hasta que no quede ninguno en la tierra que les di a ellos y a sus antepasados».

fr.L: Et j’enverrai parmi eux l’épée, la famine et la peste, jusqu’à ce qu’ils aient disparu de la terre que je leur ai donnée, à eux et à leurs pères. »
fr.B: J’enverrai contre eux l’épée, la famine et la peste, jusqu’à ce qu’ils aient disparu du pays que je leur ai donné, à eux et à leurs {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}. »
fr.R: J’enverrai contre eux la guerre, la famine et la maladie, jusqu’à ce qu’ils aient tous disparu du pays que je leur ai donné, à eux et à leurs {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}. »

pt.R: Vou mandar contra eles a guerra, a fome e a doença, até que todos eles tenham desaparecido da terra que dei a eles e aos seus antepassados."

decisions.choice: sword, famine and pestilence: the disasters of war and siege
decisions.reason: See 14:12. The three come together when an enemy besieges a city; Jeremiah names them often (21:7, 9; 27:8; 29:17-18).

decisions.choice: until they are finished off from the land I gave: the gift of the land undone
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 28:21 warns that the LORD will send pestilence "until he has finished you off from the land". The land God gave to their ancestors (7:7; 11:5) will no longer hold them.

decisions.choice: fathers: ancestors
decisions.reason: The word means the forebears of the nation, those to whom God gave the land.

decisions.choice: sword, famine and pestilence / sword, famine and plague / war, famine and disease; ancestors (Balanced, Readable); speech closes
decisions.reason: The three disasters follow the wording settled for Jeremiah. Balanced and Readable say "ancestors" (m3). God's speech, opened in verse 5, closes here.

decisions.choice: "ሰይፍ፣ ራብና ቸነፈር" at Readable too
decisions.reason: The terms list keeps one wording for this triad through Jeremiah; "ሰይፍ" for war and "ቸነፈር" for a deadly epidemic are both plain words in Amharic, so Readable needs no paraphrase.

decisions.choice: तलवार, अकाल और महामारी (L, B); युद्ध, अकाल और बीमारी (R); पुरखा (L), पूर्वज (B, R)
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's three disasters have one wording per level through this block, with महामारी for pestilence as 1 Kings 8:37; Readable says what the sword means, war, as the English Readable does. The fathers are पुरखा at L and पूर्वज (ancestors) at B and R.

decisions.choice: меч, голод и мор (L, B); война, голод и болезни (R)
decisions.reason: The three disasters of siege keep one wording per level through the book; Readable says "война" for the sword, as 16:4 does.

decisions.choice: предки (B, R); отцы (L)
decisions.reason: "Fathers" means earlier generations, so Balanced and Readable say "предки", as in 16:11.

decisions.choice: hacherev, hara'av, haddever "剣と飢饉と疫病" (L, B), "戦争とききんと疫病" (R).
decisions.reason: The JER triad (14:12).
